Q01.question: Which products should I push in my next campaign?

first_plan.objective: Identify the top products to feature in the next marketing campaign by evaluating catalog performance across realized margin, customer ratings and review count, volume share, and active stock availability in accordance with brand policy and guidelines.
success_criteria: Calculate realized margin, net revenue, unit sales, and category unit share for each product from delivered orders excluding internal customers.
Evaluate customer satisfaction metrics (average rating and review count) per product.
Verify recent stockout/incident status for candidate products using stock_events.

Apply brand profile thresholds (min_realized_margin_pct >= 55%, min_avg_rating >= 4.6, min_review_count >= 30, max_category_unit_share_pct <= 30%) to rank and recommend push candidates (stars and hidden gems) and avoid volume traps or stock-constrained items.

findings.claim: Merino Everyday Sock 3-Pack (P15) meets all brand selection thresholds, achieving an average rating of 4.78 across 291 reviews, a realized margin of 67.13%, 1325 units sold, and a category unit share of 26.05%.
Insulated Bottle 1L (P14) meets all criteria, with an average rating of 4.73 across 93 reviews, a realized margin of 60.97%, 372 units sold, and a category unit share of 17.93%.
Summit Pack 40L (P12) meets all criteria, recording an average rating of 4.67 across 54 reviews, a realized margin of 56.39%, 247 units sold, and a category unit share of 10.59%.

Historical stockout events were logged for Trail Shell Jacket (P01) from 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-27, Everyday Hoodie (P04) from 2025-04-10 to 2025-04-13, and Trail Crew Sock (P16) from 2025-09-05 to 2025-09-08, while P15, P14, and P12 had no recorded stockouts.

Top volume drivers like Classic Tee (P07) with 3219 units sold and Trail Shell Jacket (P01) with 2780 units sold generated substantial net revenue of 90758.40 and 403804.90 respectively, but both fail the selection threshold of 4.6 average rating (scoring 4.17 and 4.24) and exceed the 30% category share cap (at 53.59% and 60.00%).

raw_report_call.summary: Across the 17 catalog products evaluated against the brand's product selection thresholds (minimum average rating of 4.6, minimum review count of 30, minimum realized margin of 55%, and maximum category unit share of 30%), exactly three products satisfy all requirements for the next campaign: Merino Everyday Sock 3-Pack (P15) with an average rating of 4.78, 291 reviews, 67.13% realized margin, and 26.05% category unit share; Insulated Bottle 1L (P14) with a 4.73 average rating, 93 reviews, 60.97% realized margin, and 17.93% category unit share; and Summit Pack 40L (P12) with a 4.67 average rating, 54 reviews, 56.39% realized margin, and 10.59% category unit share. None of these three products experienced stockout incidents in the stock events log. Conversely, the catalog's largest revenue drivers—Trail Shell Jacket (P01) with 403804.90 in net revenue and Everyday Hoodie (P04) with 144882.75 in net revenue—fail the selection criteria: P01 has an average rating of 4.24 and a 60.00% category unit share (above the 30% ceiling), while P04 has a realized margin of 31.67% and an average rating of 3.79. Assumptions: Product selection thresholds (min_avg_rating 4.6, min_review_count 30, min_realized_margin_pct 55, max_category_unit_share_pct 30) were taken directly from the brand profile analysis settings; net revenue and realized margin exclude internal customers and include only delivered orders per the global glossary.

WITH category_orders AS (
    SELECT
        p.category,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN o.order_id END) AS delivered_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN o.order_id END) AS returned_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status IN ('delivered', 'returned') THEN o.order_id END) AS total_fulfilled_orders,
        ROUND(
            COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN o.order_id END)::numeric /
            NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status IN ('delivered', 'returned') THEN o.order_id END), 0) * 100,
            2
        ) AS return_rate_pct,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price ELSE 0 END) AS net_revenue
    FROM public.order_items oi
    JOIN public.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
    GROUP BY p.category
),
category_reviews AS (
    SELECT
        p.category,
        COUNT(r.review_id) AS total_reviews,
        ROUND(AVG(r.rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN r.rating <= 2 THEN 1 END) AS negative_reviews,
        ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN r.rating <= 2 THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(r.review_id), 0) * 100, 2) AS negative_review_pct
    FROM public.reviews r
    JOIN public.customers c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN public.products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
    GROUP BY p.category
)
SELECT
    co.category,
    co.delivered_orders,
    co.returned_orders,
    co.total_fulfilled_orders,
    co.return_rate_pct,
    ROUND(co.net_revenue, 2) AS net_revenue,
    cr.total_reviews,
    cr.avg_rating,
    cr.negative_reviews,
    cr.negative_review_pct
FROM category_orders co
LEFT JOIN category_reviews cr ON co.category = cr.category
ORDER BY co.return_rate_pct DESC;

WITH backpack_prod_orders AS (
    SELECT
        p.product_id,
        p.product_name,
        p.category,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN o.order_id END) AS delivered_orders,

        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status IN ('delivered', 'returned') THEN o.order_id END) AS total_fulfilled_orders,
        ROUND(
            COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN o.order_id END)::numeric /

            2
        ) AS return_rate_pct,

    JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false AND p.category = 'Backpacks'

SELECT

WITH backpack_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_date,
        o.status,
        o.promised_days,
        o.ship_days,
        CASE WHEN o.ship_days > o.promised_days THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_late,
        oi.product_id
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND p.category = 'Backpacks'
),
reviews_enriched AS (
    SELECT
        r.review_id,
        r.order_id,
        r.product_id,
        r.rating,
        CASE WHEN r.rating <= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_negative,
        bo.is_late
    FROM reviews r
    JOIN backpack_orders bo ON r.order_id = bo.order_id AND r.product_id = bo.product_id
)
SELECT
    product_id,
    is_late,
    COUNT(review_id) AS review_count,
    ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating,
    SUM(is_negative) AS negative_review_count,
    ROUND(SUM(is_negative)::numeric * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(review_id), 0), 2) AS negative_review_pct
FROM reviews_enriched
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
    (),
    (is_late),
    (product_id),
    (product_id, is_late)
)
ORDER BY product_id NULLS FIRST, is_late NULLS FIRST;

SELECT 
    se.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    se.event_type,
    se.start_date,
    se.end_date,
    (se.end_date - se.start_date) AS duration_days
FROM stock_events se
JOIN products p ON se.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.category = 'Backpacks'
ORDER BY se.start_date ASC;

SELECT

JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id

raw_report_call.summary: Preliminary: Customer unhappiness in the Backpacks category is not widespread across all backpacks or primarily driven by fulfillment delays, but is overwhelmingly concentrated in a single product: the Alder Daypack 20L (P10). Across the entire Backpacks category, the average rating is 3.77 with an 18.50% negative review rate across 692 total reviews and a 10.53% return rate across 2546 total fulfilled orders. When drilling down to the product level, P10 accounts for 123 of the category's 128 negative reviews, showing a low average rating of 3.41, a negative review rate of 29.64% across 415 reviews, and a 12.64% return rate across 1448 total fulfilled orders. In contrast, counter-evidence shows that other models perform strongly: the Commuter Pack 25L (P11) holds an average rating of 4.23 with only a 2.24% negative review rate across 223 reviews and an 8.78% return rate across 900 total fulfilled orders, while the Summit Pack 40L (P12) holds a 4.67 average rating with 0.00% negative reviews across 54 reviews and a 5.00% return rate across 260 total fulfilled orders. Furthermore, fulfillment timing is not the primary driver of negative sentiment: while 221 out of 2699 Backpack orders were late (8.19%), P10 on-time orders actually had a higher negative review rate of 29.97% across 387 reviews compared to 25.00% across 28 late reviews. Assumptions: Default order status definitions ('delivered' and 'returned') and internal customer exclusion (is_internal = false) applied per brand schema guidelines.

Assess retention and churn risk among best customers using recency and cadence (e.g. at-risk status based on order intervals).

WITH customer_stats AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        c.acquisition_channel,
        c.country,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.discount_code IS NOT NULL THEN o.order_id END) AS discounted_order_count,
        SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS net_revenue,
        SUM(oi.quantity * p.unit_cost) AS total_cost
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.acquisition_channel, c.country
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id) AS decile,
        CASE WHEN NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id) = 1 THEN 'Top Decile' ELSE 'Rest of Base (Bottom 90%)' END AS customer_group
    FROM customer_stats
),
segment_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        customer_group,
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customer_count,
        SUM(order_count) AS total_orders,
        SUM(discounted_order_count) AS total_discounted_orders,
        SUM(net_revenue) AS group_revenue,
        SUM(total_cost) AS group_cost,
        ROUND(AVG(net_revenue)::numeric, 2) AS avg_revenue_per_customer,
        ROUND(AVG(order_count)::numeric, 2) AS avg_orders_per_customer,
        ROUND((SUM(net_revenue) / SUM(order_count))::numeric, 2) AS aov,
        ROUND((SUM(discounted_order_count)::numeric / SUM(order_count) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS discount_usage_rate_pct,
        ROUND(((1 - SUM(total_cost) / SUM(net_revenue)) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS realized_margin_pct
    FROM ranked_customers
    GROUP BY customer_group
),
overall_totals AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS all_customers,
        SUM(order_count) AS all_orders,
        SUM(discounted_order_count) AS all_discounted_orders,
        SUM(net_revenue) AS all_revenue,
        SUM(total_cost) AS all_cost,
        ROUND(AVG(net_revenue)::numeric, 2) AS overall_avg_revenue_per_customer,
        ROUND(AVG(order_count)::numeric, 2) AS overall_avg_orders_per_customer,
        ROUND((SUM(net_revenue) / SUM(order_count))::numeric, 2) AS overall_aov,
        ROUND((SUM(discounted_order_count)::numeric / SUM(order_count) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS overall_discount_usage_rate_pct,
        ROUND(((1 - SUM(total_cost) / SUM(net_revenue)) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS overall_realized_margin_pct
    FROM ranked_customers
)
SELECT
    sm.customer_group,
    sm.customer_count,
    ROUND((sm.customer_count::numeric / ot.all_customers * 100)::numeric, 2) AS customer_share_pct,
    sm.total_orders,
    ROUND((sm.total_orders::numeric / ot.all_orders * 100)::numeric, 2) AS order_share_pct,
    sm.group_revenue,
    ROUND((sm.group_revenue / ot.all_revenue * 100)::numeric, 2) AS revenue_share_pct,
    sm.avg_revenue_per_customer,
    sm.avg_orders_per_customer,
    sm.aov,
    sm.discount_usage_rate_pct,
    sm.realized_margin_pct,
    ot.all_customers,
    ot.all_orders,
    ot.all_revenue,
    ot.overall_aov,
    ot.overall_avg_orders_per_customer,
    ot.overall_discount_usage_rate_pct,
    ot.overall_realized_margin_pct
FROM segment_metrics sm
CROSS JOIN overall_totals ot
ORDER BY sm.customer_group DESC;

WITH customer_rev AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        c.acquisition_channel,
        SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS net_revenue
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.acquisition_channel
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        acquisition_channel,
        net_revenue,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id ASC) AS decile
    FROM customer_rev
),
segmented_customers AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        acquisition_channel,
        CASE WHEN decile = 1 THEN 'Top Decile' ELSE 'Rest of Base' END AS customer_group
    FROM ranked_customers
)
SELECT
    sc.customer_group,
    sc.acquisition_channel,
    COUNT(sc.customer_id) AS customer_count,
    ROUND(COUNT(sc.customer_id)::numeric * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(sc.customer_id)) OVER (PARTITION BY sc.customer_group), 2) AS channel_pct_within_group,
    ROUND(COUNT(sc.customer_id)::numeric * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(sc.customer_id)) OVER (PARTITION BY sc.acquisition_channel), 2) AS top_decile_conversion_rate_by_channel,
    SUM(COUNT(sc.customer_id)) OVER (PARTITION BY sc.customer_group) AS group_total_customers
FROM segmented_customers sc
GROUP BY sc.customer_group, sc.acquisition_channel
ORDER BY sc.customer_group DESC, customer_count DESC;

WITH customer_rev AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS net_revenue
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        CASE WHEN NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id ASC) = 1 THEN 'Top Decile' ELSE 'Rest of Base' END AS customer_group
    FROM customer_rev
),
order_lines AS (
    SELECT
        rc.customer_group,
        rc.customer_id,
        p.category,
        oi.product_id,
        oi.quantity,
        (oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS line_revenue
    FROM ranked_customers rc
    JOIN public.orders o ON rc.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
)
SELECT
    customer_group,
    category,
    ROUND(SUM(line_revenue)::numeric, 2) AS category_revenue,
    SUM(quantity) AS category_units,
    ROUND(SUM(line_revenue)::numeric * 100.0 / SUM(SUM(line_revenue)) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_group), 2) AS category_revenue_share_pct,
    ROUND(SUM(quantity)::numeric * 100.0 / SUM(SUM(quantity)) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_group), 2) AS category_unit_share_pct,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS buyers_count,
    ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)::numeric * 100.0 / CASE WHEN customer_group = 'Top Decile' THEN 502 ELSE 4511 END, 2) AS group_buyer_penetration_pct
FROM order_lines
GROUP BY customer_group, category
ORDER BY customer_group DESC, category_revenue DESC;

WITH customer_rev AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS net_revenue
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        CASE WHEN NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id ASC) = 1 THEN 'Top Decile' ELSE 'Rest of Base' END AS customer_group
    FROM customer_rev
),
customer_breadth AS (
    SELECT
        rc.customer_group,
        rc.customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS distinct_categories,
        COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_products,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units
    FROM ranked_customers rc
    JOIN public.orders o ON rc.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY rc.customer_group, rc.customer_id
)
SELECT
    customer_group,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS total_customers,
    ROUND(AVG(distinct_categories)::numeric, 2) AS avg_distinct_categories,
    ROUND(AVG(distinct_products)::numeric, 2) AS avg_distinct_products,
    ROUND(AVG(total_units)::numeric, 2) AS avg_total_units,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN distinct_categories >= 3 THEN customer_id END)::numeric * 100.0 / COUNT(customer_id), 2) AS pct_multi_category_3plus,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN distinct_categories >= 2 THEN customer_id END)::numeric * 100.0 / COUNT(customer_id), 2) AS pct_multi_category_2plus
FROM customer_breadth
GROUP BY customer_group
ORDER BY customer_group DESC;

WITH customer_rev AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS net_revenue
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        net_revenue,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id ASC) AS decile
    FROM customer_rev
),
top_decile_customers AS (
    SELECT customer_id, net_revenue
    FROM ranked_customers
    WHERE decile = 1
),
dataset_max_date AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_date) AS max_order_date FROM public.orders WHERE status = 'delivered'
),
customer_orders AS (
    SELECT
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_id,
        o.order_date,
        LAG(o.order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_date) AS prev_order_date
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN top_decile_customers tdc ON o.customer_id = tdc.customer_id
    WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
),
customer_intervals AS (
    SELECT
        co.customer_id,
        COUNT(co.order_id) AS total_orders,
        MAX(co.order_date) AS last_order_date,
        (SELECT max_order_date FROM dataset_max_date) - MAX(co.order_date) AS days_since_last_order,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (co.order_date - co.prev_order_date)) AS median_inter_purchase_days
    FROM customer_orders co
    GROUP BY co.customer_id
),
customer_status AS (
    SELECT
        ci.customer_id,
        ci.total_orders,
        ci.last_order_date,
        ci.days_since_last_order,
        ci.median_inter_purchase_days,
        -- Method from KB8/KB15: at risk if days_since_last_order > GREATEST(60, 2 * median_inter_purchase_days)
        CASE 
            WHEN ci.days_since_last_order > GREATEST(60, 2 * ci.median_inter_purchase_days) THEN 'At Risk'
            ELSE 'Active'
        END AS risk_status
    FROM customer_intervals ci
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_top_decile_customers,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN risk_status = 'Active' THEN 1 END) AS active_count,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN risk_status = 'Active' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS active_share_pct,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN risk_status = 'At Risk' THEN 1 END) AS at_risk_count,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN risk_status = 'At Risk' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS at_risk_share_pct,
    ROUND(AVG(median_inter_purchase_days)::numeric, 1) AS avg_median_interval_days,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY median_inter_purchase_days)::numeric, 1) AS median_of_median_interval_days,
    ROUND(AVG(days_since_last_order)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_since_last_order,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_since_last_order)::numeric, 1) AS median_days_since_last_order,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN risk_status = 'Active' THEN days_since_last_order END)::numeric, 1) AS active_avg_recency_days,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN risk_status = 'At Risk' THEN days_since_last_order END)::numeric, 1) AS at_risk_avg_recency_days
FROM customer_status;

WITH customer_rev AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS net_revenue
    FROM public.customers c
    JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id ASC) AS decile
    FROM customer_rev
),
top_decile_customers AS (
    SELECT customer_id
    FROM ranked_customers
    WHERE decile = 1
)
SELECT
    r.rating,
    r.review_title,
    r.review_text,
    p.category,
    p.product_name
FROM public.reviews r
JOIN top_decile_customers tdc ON r.customer_id = tdc.customer_id
JOIN public.products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY r.rating ASC, r.review_date DESC
LIMIT 50;

WITH reviews_base AS (
    SELECT 
        r.rating,
        r.review_title,
        r.review_text,
        CASE WHEN r.rating >= 4 THEN 'positive'
             WHEN r.rating = 3 THEN 'neutral'
             ELSE 'negative' END AS sentiment_group
    FROM public.reviews r
    JOIN public.products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE p.product_name ILIKE '%Trail Shell Jacket%'
),
theme_counts AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS total_reviews,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS reviews_with_text,
        -- Positive themes (in 4-5 star reviews)
        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%light%' OR review_text ILIKE '%weight%') THEN 1 END) AS pos_lightweight_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%light%' OR review_text ILIKE '%weight%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS pos_lightweight_pct,
        
        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%pack%' OR review_text ILIKE '%daypack%') THEN 1 END) AS pos_packable_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%pack%' OR review_text ILIKE '%daypack%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS pos_packable_pct,

        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%rain%' OR review_text ILIKE '%commute%') THEN 1 END) AS pos_weather_commute_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%rain%' OR review_text ILIKE '%commute%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS pos_weather_commute_pct,

        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%fit%' OR review_text ILIKE '%flattering%') THEN 1 END) AS pos_fit_look_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND (review_text ILIKE '%fit%' OR review_text ILIKE '%flattering%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating >= 4 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS pos_fit_look_pct,

        -- Complaint themes (across 2-3 star reviews)
        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%pocket%' OR review_text ILIKE '%phone%') THEN 1 END) AS neg_pocket_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%pocket%' OR review_text ILIKE '%phone%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS neg_pocket_pct,

        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%tight%' OR review_text ILIKE '%small%' OR review_text ILIKE '%size%') THEN 1 END) AS neg_sizing_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%tight%' OR review_text ILIKE '%small%' OR review_text ILIKE '%size%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS neg_sizing_pct,

        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%price%' OR review_text ILIKE '%expensive%' OR review_text ILIKE '%overpriced%') THEN 1 END) AS neg_price_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%price%' OR review_text ILIKE '%expensive%' OR review_text ILIKE '%overpriced%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS neg_price_pct,

        COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%ship%' OR review_text ILIKE '%late%') THEN 1 END) AS neg_shipping_count,
        ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND (review_text ILIKE '%ship%' OR review_text ILIKE '%late%') THEN 1 END)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN rating <= 3 AND review_text IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END), 0)) * 100, 2) AS neg_shipping_pct
    FROM reviews_base
)
SELECT * FROM theme_counts;

WITH cat_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS order_month,
    p.category,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS cat_revenue,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS cat_units,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cat_orders
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  WHERE c.is_internal = false
    AND o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
cat_comparison AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-02-01' THEN cat_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS feb_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-03-01' THEN cat_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS mar_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-02-01' THEN cat_units ELSE 0 END) AS feb_units,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-03-01' THEN cat_units ELSE 0 END) AS mar_units
  FROM cat_monthly
  WHERE order_month IN ('2025-02-01', '2025-03-01')
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT
  category,
  feb_revenue,
  mar_revenue,
  ROUND(mar_revenue - feb_revenue, 2) AS rev_diff,
  ROUND(100.0 * (mar_revenue - feb_revenue) / NULLIF(feb_revenue, 0), 2) AS rev_pct_change,
  ROUND(feb_revenue / 28.0, 2) AS feb_rev_per_day,
  ROUND(mar_revenue / 31.0, 2) AS mar_rev_per_day,
  ROUND((mar_revenue / 31.0) - (feb_revenue / 28.0), 2) AS rev_per_day_diff,
  ROUND(100.0 * ((mar_revenue / 31.0) - (feb_revenue / 28.0)) / NULLIF(feb_revenue / 28.0, 0), 2) AS rev_per_day_pct_change,
  feb_units,
  mar_units,
  mar_units - feb_units AS units_diff,
  ROUND(100.0 * (mar_units - feb_units) / NULLIF(feb_units, 0), 2) AS units_pct_change,
  ROUND(feb_units::numeric / 28.0, 2) AS feb_units_per_day,
  ROUND(mar_units::numeric / 31.0, 2) AS mar_units_per_day,
  ROUND((mar_units::numeric / 31.0) - (feb_units::numeric / 28.0), 2) AS units_per_day_diff,
  ROUND(100.0 * ((mar_units::numeric / 31.0) - (feb_units::numeric / 28.0)) / NULLIF(feb_units::numeric / 28.0, 0), 2) AS units_per_day_pct_change
FROM cat_comparison
ORDER BY rev_diff ASC;

WITH prod_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    p.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    p.category,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS order_month,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS prod_revenue,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS prod_units
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  WHERE c.is_internal = false
    AND o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
),
prod_comparison AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-02-01' THEN prod_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS feb_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-03-01' THEN prod_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS mar_revenue,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-02-01' THEN prod_units ELSE 0 END) AS feb_units,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-03-01' THEN prod_units ELSE 0 END) AS mar_units
  FROM prod_monthly
  WHERE order_month IN ('2025-02-01', '2025-03-01')
  GROUP BY product_id, product_name, category
)
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_name,
  category,
  feb_revenue,
  mar_revenue,
  ROUND(mar_revenue - feb_revenue, 2) AS rev_diff,
  ROUND(100.0 * (mar_revenue - feb_revenue) / NULLIF(feb_revenue, 0), 2) AS rev_pct_change,
  ROUND(feb_revenue / 28.0, 2) AS feb_rev_per_day,
  ROUND(mar_revenue / 31.0, 2) AS mar_rev_per_day,
  ROUND((mar_revenue / 31.0) - (feb_revenue / 28.0), 2) AS rev_per_day_diff,
  ROUND(100.0 * ((mar_revenue / 31.0) - (feb_revenue / 28.0)) / NULLIF(feb_revenue / 28.0, 0), 2) AS rev_per_day_pct_change,
  feb_units,
  mar_units,
  mar_units - feb_units AS units_diff,
  ROUND(100.0 * (mar_units - feb_units) / NULLIF(feb_units, 0), 2) AS units_pct_change
FROM prod_comparison
ORDER BY rev_diff ASC
LIMIT 15;

WITH order_agg AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS order_month,
    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_date,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS order_net_revenue,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS order_units
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  WHERE c.is_internal = false
    AND o.status = 'delivered'
    AND o.order_date >= '2025-02-01'
    AND o.order_date < '2025-04-01'
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
),
first_orders AS (
  SELECT
    o.customer_id,
    MIN(o.order_date) AS first_delivered_order_date
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE c.is_internal = false
    AND o.status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY 1
),
order_classified AS (
  SELECT
    oa.*,
    CASE
      WHEN oa.order_date = fo.first_delivered_order_date THEN 'new'
      ELSE 'existing'
    END AS customer_type
  FROM order_agg oa
  JOIN first_orders fo ON oa.customer_id = fo.customer_id
),
monthly_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    order_month,
    CASE WHEN order_month = '2025-02-01' THEN 28 ELSE 31 END AS days_in_month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers,
    ROUND(SUM(order_net_revenue), 2) AS total_revenue,
    SUM(order_units) AS total_units,
    ROUND(SUM(order_net_revenue) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS aov,
    ROUND(SUM(order_units)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS units_per_order,
    -- new customers
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN customer_type = 'new' THEN order_id END) AS new_orders,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN customer_type = 'new' THEN order_net_revenue END), 0), 2) AS new_revenue,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN customer_type = 'new' THEN order_net_revenue END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN customer_type = 'new' THEN order_id END), 0), 0), 2) AS new_aov,
    -- existing customers
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN customer_type = 'existing' THEN order_id END) AS existing_orders,

WITH daily_p01 AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_date,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS daily_rev,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS daily_units
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  WHERE c.is_internal = false
    AND o.status = 'delivered'
    AND oi.product_id = 'P01'
    AND o.order_date >= '2025-02-01'
    AND o.order_date <= '2025-03-31'
  GROUP BY o.order_date
),
calendar AS (
  SELECT d::date AS order_date
  FROM generate_series('2025-02-01'::date, '2025-03-31'::date, '1 day'::interval) d
),
p01_full AS (
  SELECT
    c.order_date,
    COALESCE(dp.daily_rev, 0) AS daily_rev,
    COALESCE(dp.daily_units, 0) AS daily_units,
    CASE 
      WHEN c.order_date >= '2025-02-01' AND c.order_date <= '2025-02-28' THEN 'Feb'
      WHEN c.order_date >= '2025-03-01' AND c.order_date <= '2025-03-12' THEN 'Mar_pre_stockout'
      WHEN c.order_date >= '2025-03-13' AND c.order_date <= '2025-03-31' THEN 'Mar_stockout'
    END AS period
  FROM calendar c
  LEFT JOIN daily_p01 dp ON c.order_date = dp.order_date
)
SELECT
  period,
  COUNT(*) AS days,
  ROUND(SUM(daily_rev), 2) AS total_revenue,
  SUM(daily_units) AS total_units,
  ROUND(AVG(daily_rev), 2) AS rev_per_day,
  ROUND(AVG(daily_units), 2) AS units_per_day
FROM p01_full
GROUP BY period
ORDER BY MIN(order_date);

WITH p01_daily AS (
  SELECT
    d::date AS order_date,
    COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) AS daily_rev,
    COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS daily_units
  FROM generate_series('2025-02-01'::date, '2025-03-31'::date, '1 day'::interval) d
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON d::date = o.order_date AND o.status = 'delivered'
  LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND c.is_internal = false
  LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND oi.product_id = 'P01'
  GROUP BY d::date
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-02-01' AND order_date <= '2025-02-28' THEN daily_rev ELSE 0 END), 2) AS feb_rev,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-02-01' AND order_date <= '2025-02-28' THEN daily_rev ELSE 0 END) / 28.0, 2) AS feb_rev_per_day,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-02-01' AND order_date <= '2025-02-28' THEN daily_units ELSE 0 END) AS feb_units,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-02-01' AND order_date <= '2025-02-28' THEN daily_units ELSE 0 END) / 28.0, 2) AS feb_units_per_day,
    
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-03-03' AND order_date <= '2025-03-27' THEN daily_rev ELSE 0 END), 2) AS stockout_rev,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-03-03' AND order_date <= '2025-03-27' THEN daily_rev ELSE 0 END) / 25.0, 2) AS stockout_rev_per_day,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-03-03' AND order_date <= '2025-03-27' THEN daily_units ELSE 0 END) AS stockout_units,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN order_date >= '2025-03-03' AND order_date <= '2025-03-27' THEN daily_units ELSE 0 END) / 25.0, 2) AS stockout_units_per_day,

findings.claim: Total delivered net revenue decreased from 93616.30 in February (28 days) to 93261.80 in March (31 days), representing a revenue difference of -354.50 or a decrease of -0.38%, while revenue per day dropped from 3343.44 to 3008.45, a difference of -334.99 or -10.02%.
While total delivered orders increased from 856 to 971 (an increase of 115 orders or 13.43%), average order value fell from 109.36 to 96.05, a decline of -13.31 or -12.17%.

Delivered revenue from new customers dropped from 61265.70 in February to 44138.15 in March (a decline of -17127.55 or -27.96%), with new customer orders falling from 600 to 487 (a difference of -113), whereas existing customer revenue increased from 32350.60 to 49123.65 (a gain of 16773.05 or 51.85%).

Across product categories, Jackets experienced a revenue drop from 38690.00 to 24517.15 (a difference of -14172.85 or -36.63%) and a daily revenue drop from 1381.79 to 790.88 (-42.76%), while all other major categories grew in absolute monthly revenue.

The revenue decline in Jackets was driven by the Trail Shell Jacket (P01), which fell from 24212.50 in February to 7561.75 in March, a difference of -16650.75 or -68.77%, with units falling from 164 to 51 (a decrease of -113).
The Trail Shell Jacket (P01) experienced an official stockout event of 25 days from 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-27.

During the 25-day stockout period, P01 generated 1192.00 in revenue (47.68 per day across 8 units), compared to 6369.75 across the 6 in-stock days of March (1061.63 per day across 43 units) and 24212.50 across February (864.73 per day across 164 units), resulting in an estimated lost revenue of 20426.25 against the February run rate and 25348.75 against the March in-stock run rate.

Total marketing spend decreased from 6332.35 in February to 3865.63 in March (a reduction of -2466.72 or -38.95%), driven primarily by a cut in paid social spend from 2741.48 to 424.46 (a reduction of -2317.02 or -84.52%).

Total customer signups fell from 258 in February (9.21 per day) to 222 in March (7.16 per day), an overall drop of -36 signups (-13.95%), heavily concentrated in paid social signups which fell from 66 to 13 (-53 signups or -80.30%).

raw_report_call.summary:
In March 2025, total delivered net revenue fell slightly on an absolute monthly basis from 93616.30 to 93261.80 (a decline of -354.50 or -0.38%), but dropped substantially on a per-day normalized basis from 3343.44 to 3008.45 (a drop of -334.99 per day or -10.02%). Although delivered order volume actually increased from 856 to 971 (an increase of 115 orders or 13.43%), average order value collapsed from 109.36 to 96.05 (-12.17%).

This downturn was driven by two interacting causes:
1. Supply-side stockout: The brand's top product, the Trail Shell Jacket (P01), was out of stock for 25 days (2025-03-03 to 2025-03-27). This single product experienced a revenue collapse of -16650.75 (-68.77%), falling from 24212.50 in February (864.73 per day) to 7561.75 in March (243.93 per day). Estimated lost revenue on P01 during the stockout reached 20426.25 against February daily rates and 25348.75 against March in-stock rates.
2. Demand-side marketing contraction: Marketing spend dropped from 6332.35 to 3865.63 (-38.95%), driven by an -84.52% cut in paid social spend (from 2741.48 to 424.46). Consequently, paid social signups plummeted from 66 to 13 (-80.30%), total new customer revenue contracted from 61265.70 to 44138.15 (-27.96%), and new customer orders fell from 600 to 487 (-113 orders).

Counter-evidence and offsetting strength: Existing customer revenue grew strongly from 32350.60 to 49123.65 (a gain of 16773.05 or 51.85%), and other categories such as Backpacks (+6236.90) and Hoodies (+4601.70) grew substantially, which prevented an even larger net top-line collapse.

Assumptions: Analysis covers February 1 to March 31, 2025; internal customers are excluded per global glossary conventions; net revenue includes only delivered orders. Per-day normalization accounts for February having 28 days and March having 31 days.

findings.claim: Total delivered net revenue decreased from 93616.30 in February (28 days) to 93261.80 in March (31 days), representing a revenue difference of -354.50 or a decrease of -0.38%, while revenue per day dropped from 3343.44 to 3008.45, a difference of -334.99 or -10.02%.
While total delivered orders increased from 856 to 971 (an increase of 115 orders or 13.43%), average order value fell from 109.36 to 96.05, a decline of -13.31 or -12.17%.

Delivered revenue from new customers dropped from 61265.70 in February to 44138.15 in March (a decline of -17127.55 or -27.96%), with new customer orders falling from 600 to 487 (a difference of -113), whereas existing customer revenue increased from 32350.60 to 49123.65 (a gain of 16773.05 or 51.85%).

Across product categories, Jackets experienced a revenue drop from 38690.00 to 24517.15 (a difference of -14172.85 or -36.63%) and a daily revenue drop from 1381.79 to 790.88 (-42.76%), while all other major categories grew in absolute monthly revenue.

The revenue decline in Jackets was driven by the Trail Shell Jacket (P01), which fell from 24212.50 in February to 7561.75 in March, a difference of -16650.75 or -68.77%, with units falling from 164 to 51 (a decrease of -113).
The Trail Shell Jacket (P01) experienced an official stockout event of 25 days from 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-27.

During the 25-day stockout period, P01 generated 1192.00 in revenue (47.68 per day across 8 units), compared to 6369.75 across the 6 in-stock days of March (1061.63 per day across 43 units) and 24212.50 across February (864.73 per day across 164 units), resulting in an estimated lost revenue of 20426.25 against the February run rate and 25348.75 against the March in-stock run rate.

Total marketing spend decreased from 6332.35 in February to 3865.63 in March (a reduction of -2466.72 or -38.95%), driven primarily by a cut in paid social spend from 2741.48 to 424.46 (a reduction of -2317.02 or -84.52%).

Total customer signups fell from 258 in February (9.21 per day) to 222 in March (7.16 per day), an overall drop of -36 signups (-13.95%), heavily concentrated in paid social signups which fell from 66 to 13 (-53 signups or -80.30%).

actions: Implement inventory safety stock thresholds and replenishment triggers for core hero products like the Trail Shell Jacket (P01) to prevent extended out-of-stock windows.
Stabilize paid acquisition channels, specifically avoiding sharp month-over-month reductions in paid social spend, while continuing to leverage email and referral growth.

WITH valid_orders AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_date
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = FALSE
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
),
benchmarks AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_date) AS benchmark_date FROM valid_orders
),
order_lags AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        order_date,
        LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS prev_order_date
    FROM valid_orders
),
customer_intervals AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (order_date - prev_order_date)) AS median_gap_days,
        COUNT(*) + 1 AS order_count_check, -- not strictly needed, let's do clean count
        MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date
    FROM order_lags
    WHERE prev_order_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_order_counts AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_delivered_orders,
        MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date,
        MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date
    FROM valid_orders
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_cadence AS (
    SELECT
        coc.customer_id,
        coc.total_delivered_orders,
        coc.first_order_date,
        coc.last_order_date,
        ci.median_gap_days,
        b.benchmark_date,
        (b.benchmark_date - coc.last_order_date) AS days_since_last_order,
        GREATEST(60, 2.0 * ci.median_gap_days) AS risk_threshold_days
    FROM customer_order_counts coc
    CROSS JOIN benchmarks b
    LEFT JOIN customer_intervals ci ON coc.customer_id = ci.customer_id
),
risk_classification AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        CASE
            WHEN total_delivered_orders >= 3 AND days_since_last_order > risk_threshold_days THEN 'at_risk'
            WHEN total_delivered_orders >= 3 AND days_since_last_order <= risk_threshold_days THEN 'active_repeat'
            WHEN total_delivered_orders = 2 THEN 'two_order_customer'
            ELSE 'one_order_customer'
        END AS churn_risk_status
    FROM customer_cadence
)
SELECT
    churn_risk_status,
    COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_customers,
    ROUND(AVG(total_delivered_orders)::numeric, 2) AS avg_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(median_gap_days)::numeric, 2) AS avg_median_gap_days,
    ROUND(AVG(days_since_last_order)::numeric, 2) AS avg_days_since_last_order,
    MIN(benchmark_date) AS benchmark_date
FROM risk_classification
GROUP BY churn_risk_status
ORDER BY customer_count DESC;

),

),

    FROM order_lags
    WHERE prev_order_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_summary AS (
    SELECT
        vo.customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT vo.order_id) AS total_orders,
        b.benchmark_date - MAX(vo.order_date) AS days_since_last_order,
        cg.median_gap_days
    FROM valid_orders vo
    CROSS JOIN benchmarks b
    LEFT JOIN customer_gaps cg ON vo.customer_id = cg.customer_id
    GROUP BY vo.customer_id, b.benchmark_date, cg.median_gap_days
),
at_risk_customers AS (
    SELECT customer_id
    FROM customer_summary
    WHERE total_orders >= 3
      AND days_since_last_order > 2 * median_gap_days
),
at_risk_category_spend AS (
    SELECT
        p.category,
        ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS category_net_revenue,
        SUM(oi.quantity) AS category_units,
        COUNT(DISTINCT arc.customer_id) AS buying_customers
    FROM at_risk_customers arc
    JOIN valid_orders vo ON arc.customer_id = vo.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON vo.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY p.category
),
total_at_risk AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_at_risk_customers,
        SUM(category_net_revenue) AS total_rev,
        SUM(category_units) AS total_units
    FROM at_risk_category_spend, at_risk_customers
    GROUP BY ()
)
SELECT
    acs.category,
    acs.category_net_revenue,
    ROUND(acs.category_net_revenue * 100.0 / tr.total_rev, 2) AS rev_share_pct,
    acs.category_units,
    ROUND(acs.category_units::numeric * 100.0 / tr.total_units, 2) AS unit_share_pct,
    acs.buying_customers,
    ROUND(acs.buying_customers::numeric * 100.0 / tr.total_at_risk_customers, 2) AS customer_penetration_pct
FROM at_risk_category_spend acs
CROSS JOIN total_at_risk tr
ORDER BY acs.category_net_revenue DESC;

WITH valid_orders AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_date,
        o.discount_code
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = FALSE

order_lags AS (

),
customer_gaps AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (order_date - prev_order_date)) AS median_gap_days
    FROM order_lags
    WHERE prev_order_date IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_summary AS (
    SELECT
        vo.customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT vo.order_id) AS total_orders,
        b.benchmark_date - MAX(vo.order_date) AS days_since_last_order,
        cg.median_gap_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN vo.discount_code IS NOT NULL AND vo.discount_code <> '' THEN vo.order_id END) AS discounted_orders
    FROM valid_orders vo
    CROSS JOIN benchmarks b
    LEFT JOIN customer_gaps cg ON vo.customer_id = cg.customer_id
    GROUP BY vo.customer_id, b.benchmark_date, cg.median_gap_days
),
customer_financials AS (
    SELECT
        vo.customer_id,
        ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS net_revenue,
        ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * p.unit_cost), 2) AS cogs,
        ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * (p.list_price - oi.unit_price)), 2) AS total_discount_amount
    FROM valid_orders vo
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON vo.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    GROUP BY vo.customer_id
),
customer_deciles AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        net_revenue,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY net_revenue DESC, customer_id) AS rev_decile
    FROM customer_financials
),
at_risk_customers AS (
    SELECT
        cs.customer_id,
        cs.total_orders,
        cs.days_since_last_order,
        cs.median_gap_days,
        cs.discounted_orders,
        cf.net_revenue,
        cf.cogs,
        cf.total_discount_amount,
        cd.rev_decile
    FROM customer_summary cs
    JOIN customer_financials cf ON cs.customer_id = cf.customer_id
    JOIN customer_deciles cd ON cs.customer_id = cd.customer_id
    WHERE cs.total_orders >= 3
      AND cs.days_since_last_order > 2 * cs.median_gap_days
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_at_risk_customers,
    ROUND(SUM(net_revenue), 2) AS total_at_risk_net_revenue,
    ROUND(AVG(net_revenue), 2) AS avg_net_revenue,
    ROUND(AVG(total_orders), 2) AS avg_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(net_revenue / total_orders), 2) AS avg_aov,
    ROUND(SUM(net_revenue - cogs) * 100.0 / SUM(net_revenue), 2) AS realized_margin_pct,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN rev_decile = 1 THEN 1 END) AS top_decile_customers,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN rev_decile = 1 THEN 1 END)::numeric * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS top_decile_pct,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN discounted_orders = 0 THEN 1 END) AS never_discounted_customers,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN discounted_orders = 0 THEN 1 END)::numeric * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS never_discounted_pct,
    ROUND(AVG(discounted_orders::numeric / total_orders) * 100.0, 2) AS avg_discounted_order_pct
FROM at_risk_customers;

overall_one_time AS (

raw_report_call.summary: Customers about to churn comprise two distinct cohorts: an at-risk core of 319 to 345 high-cadence repeat buyers whose days since last order (averaging 145.00 days) substantially exceed their historical cadence (average median gap of 42.31 days), and a broader pool of 1862 one-time buyers averaging 132.48 days since purchase, of whom 561 have lapsed beyond 180 days. The at-risk repeat cohort is highly valuable, generating 163614.90 in net revenue at a 56.25% realized margin, with 61 customers (17.68%) in the top decile and 31.88% having never redeemed a discount code. For outreach, Alder & Fox should avoid heavy discounting—adhering to its brand policy to avoid training best customers to wait for discounts—and instead deploy automated email flows emphasizing durability, repairability, and category replenishment across core categories like Tees, Hoodies, and Jackets. Assumptions: Repeat customer churn risk is defined using individual purchase intervals (days since last order exceeding 1.5 to 2.0 times customer median order gap); benchmark date is 2025-12-31; internal accounts (is_internal = true) and non-delivered orders are excluded.
cannot_determine: Customer-specific unsubscribes, email engagement rates, and open rates are not tracked in the orders or customers database tables.
Customer churn reasons (e.g., product dissatisfaction versus lack of need) cannot be definitively verified from order logs alone without comprehensive qualitative exit surveys.

input.sql:
WITH max_date AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_date) AS max_order_date FROM orders
),
bounds AS (
    -- acquisition_value_window_days = 90
    -- cohort_end: MAX(orders.order_date) - 90 days, rounded down to end of last complete calendar month
    -- marketing spend is recorded per calendar month.
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', max_order_date - INTERVAL '90 days') - INTERVAL '1 day' AS cohort_end_date,
        DATE '2025-01-01' AS cohort_start_date
    FROM max_date
),
cohort_customers AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        c.signup_date,
        c.acquisition_channel,
        c.country
    FROM customers c
    CROSS JOIN bounds b
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND c.signup_date >= b.cohort_start_date
      AND c.signup_date <= b.cohort_end_date
),
cust_orders_90d AS (
    SELECT 
        cc.customer_id,
        cc.acquisition_channel,
        o.order_id,
        o.order_date,
        o.status
    FROM cohort_customers cc
    LEFT JOIN orders o 
        ON cc.customer_id = o.customer_id 
        AND o.order_date >= cc.signup_date 
        AND o.order_date < cc.signup_date + INTERVAL '90 days'
),
cust_delivered_lines_90d AS (
    SELECT 
        co.customer_id,
        co.acquisition_channel,
        co.order_id,
        oi.quantity * oi.unit_price AS line_net_revenue,
        oi.quantity * p.unit_cost AS line_cost
    FROM cust_orders_90d co
    JOIN order_items oi ON co.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE co.status = 'delivered'
),
customer_summary AS (
    SELECT 
        cc.customer_id,
        cc.acquisition_channel,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.status = 'delivered' THEN co.order_id END) AS delivered_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.status = 'returned' THEN co.order_id END) AS returned_orders,
        COALESCE(SUM(cdl.line_net_revenue), 0) AS net_revenue_90d,
        COALESCE(SUM(cdl.line_cost), 0) AS cost_90d,
        COALESCE(SUM(cdl.line_net_revenue), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(cdl.line_cost), 0) AS gross_profit_90d
    FROM cohort_customers cc
    LEFT JOIN cust_orders_90d co ON cc.customer_id = co.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN cust_delivered_lines_90d cdl ON cc.customer_id = cdl.customer_id AND co.order_id = cdl.order_id
    GROUP BY cc.customer_id, cc.acquisition_channel
),
channel_spend AS (
    SELECT 
        ms.channel AS acquisition_channel,
        SUM(ms.spend_usd) AS total_spend
    FROM marketing_spend ms
    CROSS JOIN bounds b
    WHERE ms.month >= b.cohort_start_date
      AND ms.month <= DATE_TRUNC('month', b.cohort_end_date)
    GROUP BY ms.channel
),
channel_agg AS (
    SELECT 
        cs.acquisition_channel,
        COUNT(cs.customer_id) AS cohort_size,
        SUM(cs.net_revenue_90d) AS channel_net_revenue_90d,
        SUM(cs.gross_profit_90d) AS channel_gross_profit_90d,
        SUM(cs.delivered_orders) AS total_delivered_orders,
        SUM(cs.returned_orders) AS total_returned_orders,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN cs.delivered_orders >= 1 THEN 1 END) AS acquired_paying_customers,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN cs.delivered_orders >= 2 THEN 1 END) AS repeat_customers
    FROM customer_summary cs
    GROUP BY cs.acquisition_channel
),
all_channels AS (
    SELECT 
        COALESCE(ca.acquisition_channel, s.acquisition_channel) AS channel,
        COALESCE(ca.cohort_size, 0) AS cohort_size,
        COALESCE(s.total_spend, 0) AS spend_usd,
        COALESCE(ca.channel_net_revenue_90d, 0) AS net_revenue_90d,
        COALESCE(ca.channel_gross_profit_90d, 0) AS gross_profit_90d,
        COALESCE(ca.total_delivered_orders, 0) AS delivered_orders,
        COALESCE(ca.total_returned_orders, 0) AS returned_orders,
        COALESCE(ca.acquired_paying_customers, 0) AS paying_customers,
        COALESCE(ca.repeat_customers, 0) AS repeat_customers
    FROM channel_agg ca
    FULL OUTER JOIN channel_spend s ON ca.acquisition_channel = s.acquisition_channel
)
SELECT 
    b.cohort_start_date,
    b.cohort_end_date,
    ac.channel,
    ac.cohort_size,
    ac.spend_usd,
    ROUND(ac.spend_usd / NULLIF(ac.cohort_size, 0), 2) AS cac_per_signup,
    ROUND(ac.spend_usd / NULLIF(ac.paying_customers, 0), 2) AS cac_per_paying_customer,
    ROUND(ac.net_revenue_90d, 2) AS net_revenue_90d,
    ROUND(ac.gross_profit_90d, 2) AS gross_profit_90d,
    ROUND(ac.net_revenue_90d / NULLIF(ac.cohort_size, 0), 2) AS net_rev_per_cohort_member,
    ROUND(ac.gross_profit_90d / NULLIF(ac.cohort_size, 0), 2) AS gp_per_cohort_member,
    ROUND(ac.gross_profit_90d / NULLIF(ac.spend_usd, 0), 2) AS gp_per_cac_dollar,
    ROUND(ac.repeat_customers::numeric / NULLIF(ac.paying_customers, 0) * 100, 2) AS repeat_rate_pct_of_paying,
    ROUND(ac.repeat_customers::numeric / NULLIF(ac.cohort_size, 0) * 100, 2) AS repeat_rate_pct_of_signups,
    ROUND(ac.returned_orders::numeric / NULLIF(ac.delivered_orders + ac.returned_orders, 0) * 100, 2) AS return_rate_pct,
    ROUND((ac.gross_profit_90d / NULLIF(ac.net_revenue_90d, 0)) * 100, 2) AS realized_margin_pct
FROM all_channels ac
CROSS JOIN bounds b
ORDER BY ac.channel;

WITH max_date AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_date) AS max_order_date FROM orders
),
bounds AS (
    SELECT 
        (DATE_TRUNC('month', max_order_date - INTERVAL '90 days') - INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS cohort_end_date,
        DATE '2025-01-01' AS cohort_start_date
    FROM max_date
),
cohort_customers AS (
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        c.acquisition_channel,
        c.signup_date
    FROM customers c
    CROSS JOIN bounds b
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND c.signup_date >= b.cohort_start_date
      AND c.signup_date <= b.cohort_end_date
),
cohort_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        cc.acquisition_channel,
        cc.customer_id,
        o.order_id,
        o.order_date,
        o.status,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price ELSE 0 END) AS order_net_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN oi.quantity * p.unit_cost ELSE 0 END) AS order_cost
    FROM cohort_customers cc
    JOIN orders o ON cc.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE o.order_date >= cc.signup_date
      AND o.order_date <= cc.signup_date + INTERVAL '90 days'
    GROUP BY cc.acquisition_channel, cc.customer_id, o.order_id, o.order_date, o.status
),
cust_summary AS (
    SELECT 
        cc.acquisition_channel,
        cc.customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.status = 'delivered' THEN co.order_id END) AS delivered_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.status IN ('delivered', 'returned') THEN co.order_id END) AS valid_orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.status = 'returned' THEN co.order_id END) AS returned_orders,
        COALESCE(SUM(co.order_net_rev), 0) AS cust_net_rev,
        COALESCE(SUM(co.order_cost), 0) AS cust_cost
    FROM cohort_customers cc
    LEFT JOIN cohort_orders co ON cc.customer_id = co.customer_id
    GROUP BY cc.acquisition_channel, cc.customer_id
),
channel_agg AS (
    SELECT 
        acquisition_channel AS channel,
        COUNT(customer_id) AS cohort_size,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN delivered_orders > 0 THEN customer_id END) AS paying_customers,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN delivered_orders > 1 THEN customer_id END) AS repeat_customers,
        SUM(cust_net_rev) AS net_revenue_90d,
        SUM(cust_cost) AS cost_90d,
        SUM(cust_net_rev) - SUM(cust_cost) AS gross_profit_90d,
        SUM(delivered_orders) AS total_delivered_orders,
        SUM(returned_orders) AS total_returned_orders,
        SUM(valid_orders) AS total_valid_orders
    FROM cust_summary
    GROUP BY acquisition_channel
),
channel_spend AS (
    SELECT 
        ms.channel,
        SUM(ms.spend_usd) AS spend_usd
    FROM marketing_spend ms
    CROSS JOIN bounds b
    WHERE ms.month >= b.cohort_start_date
      AND ms.month <= b.cohort_end_date
    GROUP BY ms.channel
),
combined AS (
    SELECT 
        ca.channel,
        ca.cohort_size,
        ca.paying_customers,
        ca.repeat_customers,
        COALESCE(cs.spend_usd, 0) AS spend_usd,
        ca.net_revenue_90d,
        ca.gross_profit_90d,
        ca.total_delivered_orders,
        ca.total_returned_orders,
        ca.total_valid_orders
    FROM channel_agg ca
    LEFT JOIN channel_spend cs ON ca.channel = cs.channel
),
with_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        channel,
        cohort_size,
        paying_customers,
        repeat_customers,
        spend_usd,
        net_revenue_90d,
        gross_profit_90d,
        total_delivered_orders,
        total_returned_orders,
        total_valid_orders
    FROM combined
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        'TOTAL / BLENDED' AS channel,
        SUM(cohort_size) AS cohort_size,
        SUM(paying_customers) AS paying_customers,
        SUM(repeat_customers) AS repeat_customers,
        SUM(spend_usd) AS spend_usd,
        SUM(net_revenue_90d) AS net_revenue_90d,
        SUM(gross_profit_90d) AS gross_profit_90d,
        SUM(total_delivered_orders) AS total_delivered_orders,
        SUM(total_returned_orders) AS total_returned_orders,
        SUM(total_valid_orders) AS total_valid_orders
    FROM combined
)
SELECT 
    channel,
    cohort_size,
    paying_customers,
    repeat_customers,
    ROUND(spend_usd, 2) AS spend_usd,
    ROUND(spend_usd / NULLIF(cohort_size, 0), 2) AS cac_per_signup,
    ROUND(spend_usd / NULLIF(paying_customers, 0), 2) AS cac_per_paying_customer,
    ROUND(net_revenue_90d, 2) AS net_revenue_90d,
    ROUND(gross_profit_90d, 2) AS gross_profit_90d,
    ROUND(net_revenue_90d / NULLIF(cohort_size, 0), 2) AS net_rev_per_cohort_member,
    ROUND(gross_profit_90d / NULLIF(cohort_size, 0), 2) AS gp_per_cohort_member,
    ROUND(gross_profit_90d / NULLIF(spend_usd, 0), 2) AS gp_per_cac_dollar,
    ROUND(repeat_customers::numeric / NULLIF(paying_customers, 0) * 100, 2) AS repeat_rate_pct_of_paying,
    ROUND(repeat_customers::numeric / NULLIF(cohort_size, 0) * 100, 2) AS repeat_rate_pct_of_signups,
    ROUND(total_returned_orders::numeric / NULLIF(total_valid_orders, 0) * 100, 2) AS return_rate_pct,
    ROUND((gross_profit_90d / NULLIF(net_revenue_90d, 0)) * 100, 2) AS realized_margin_pct
FROM with_totals
ORDER BY CASE WHEN channel = 'TOTAL / BLENDED' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END, spend_usd DESC;

raw_report_call.summary: Preliminary: Referral and email_signup bring the highest-quality customers in terms of 90-day value and retention, while among paid acquisition channels, paid_search clearly outperforms paid_social. For the cohort of customers signing up between 2025-01-01 and 2025-09-30 evaluated over a 90-day window, referral generated 116.97 USD in gross profit per cohort member and a 54.17% repeat purchase rate among paying customers (52.30% of signups), and email_signup generated 90.17 USD in gross profit per cohort member with a 49.54% repeat rate among paying customers (47.90% of signups). Within dedicated paid channels, paid_search achieved 86.01 USD in gross profit per cohort member, a 43.65% repeat rate among paying customers, and a 7.69% return rate at a 30.14 USD CAC per paying customer (3.00 USD gross profit per CAC dollar). Conversely, paid_social exhibited the lowest customer quality and performance: 62.90 USD gross profit per cohort member, a 32.01% repeat rate among paying customers, a return rate of 12.74%, and only 1.69 USD gross profit per CAC dollar, despite taking the largest share of spend at 24026.83 USD. Counter-evidence to immediately reallocating all budget away from paid_social is that paid_social delivered the largest volume of cohort signups (644 members and 581 paying customers), and marginal saturation curves across channels were not analyzed before this investigation was stopped. Reallocating budget toward paid_search and organic/referral initiatives aligns with the brand's objective to reduce reliance on paid social, but shifts should be executed gradually. input.sql:
SELECT 
    promo_code, 
    description, 
    start_date, 
    end_date, 
    (end_date - start_date + 1) AS sale_days,
    discount_pct 
FROM public.promotions 
WHERE (start_date >= '2025-07-01' AND start_date <= '2025-07-31') 
   OR description ILIKE '%july%';

WITH promo_info AS (
    SELECT 
        start_date,
        end_date,
        (end_date - start_date + 1) AS sale_days
    FROM public.promotions
    WHERE promo_code = 'SUMMER25'
),
windows AS (
    SELECT
        p.start_date,
        p.end_date,
        p.sale_days,
        -- baseline: 30 days prior to sale start (from brand settings: baseline_days = 30)
        (p.start_date - INTERVAL '30 days')::date AS baseline_start,
        (p.start_date - INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS baseline_end,
        30 AS baseline_days,
        -- post-sale horizons
        (p.end_date + INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS post14_start,
        (p.end_date + INTERVAL '14 days')::date AS post14_end,
        14 AS post14_days,
        (p.end_date + INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS post28_start,
        (p.end_date + INTERVAL '28 days')::date AS post28_end,
        28 AS post28_days,
        (p.end_date + INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS post42_start,
        (p.end_date + INTERVAL '42 days')::date AS post42_end,
        42 AS post42_days
    FROM promo_info p
),
order_lines AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        o.order_date,
        o.status,
        oi.quantity,
        oi.unit_price,
        oi.discount_pct,
        pr.unit_cost,
        pr.list_price,
        (oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS line_net_rev,
        (oi.quantity * pr.unit_cost) AS line_cogs,
        (oi.quantity * (pr.list_price - oi.unit_price)) AS line_discount_cost
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.products pr ON oi.product_id = pr.product_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = false
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
),
period_metrics AS (
    -- Baseline (30d)
    SELECT
        'Baseline (30d)' AS period_name,
        1 AS sort_order,
        w.baseline_start AS start_date,
        w.baseline_end AS end_date,
        w.baseline_days AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.baseline_start AND w.baseline_end
    GROUP BY w.baseline_start, w.baseline_end, w.baseline_days

    UNION ALL

    -- Sale (10d)
    SELECT
        'Sale (10d)' AS period_name,
        2 AS sort_order,
        w.start_date AS start_date,
        w.end_date AS end_date,
        w.sale_days AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.start_date AND w.end_date
    GROUP BY w.start_date, w.end_date, w.sale_days

    UNION ALL

    -- Post-Sale 14d
    SELECT
        'Post-Sale (14d)' AS period_name,
        3 AS sort_order,
        w.post14_start AS start_date,
        w.post14_end AS end_date,
        w.post14_days AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.post14_start AND w.post14_end
    GROUP BY w.post14_start, w.post14_end, w.post14_days

    UNION ALL

    -- Post-Sale 28d
    SELECT
        'Post-Sale (28d)' AS period_name,
        4 AS sort_order,
        w.post28_start AS start_date,
        w.post28_end AS end_date,
        w.post28_days AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.post28_start AND w.post28_end
    GROUP BY w.post28_start, w.post28_end, w.post28_days

    UNION ALL

    -- Post-Sale 42d
    SELECT
        'Post-Sale (42d)' AS period_name,
        5 AS sort_order,
        w.post42_start AS start_date,
        w.post42_end AS end_date,
        w.post42_days AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.post42_start AND w.post42_end
    GROUP BY w.post42_start, w.post42_end, w.post42_days

    UNION ALL

    -- Combined: Sale + Post 14d (24d)
    SELECT
        'Combined: Sale + Post 14d (24d)' AS period_name,
        6 AS sort_order,
        w.start_date AS start_date,
        w.post14_end AS end_date,
        (w.sale_days + w.post14_days) AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.start_date AND w.post14_end
    GROUP BY w.start_date, w.post14_end, w.sale_days, w.post14_days

    UNION ALL

    -- Combined: Sale + Post 28d (38d)
    SELECT
        'Combined: Sale + Post 28d (38d)' AS period_name,
        7 AS sort_order,
        w.start_date AS start_date,
        w.post28_end AS end_date,
        (w.sale_days + w.post28_days) AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.start_date AND w.post28_end
    GROUP BY w.start_date, w.post28_end, w.sale_days, w.post28_days

    UNION ALL

    -- Combined: Sale + Post 42d (52d)
    SELECT
        'Combined: Sale + Post 42d (52d)' AS period_name,
        8 AS sort_order,
        w.start_date AS start_date,
        w.post42_end AS end_date,
        (w.sale_days + w.post42_days) AS num_days,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(ol.line_net_rev - ol.line_cogs) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(ol.line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM windows w
    LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_date BETWEEN w.start_date AND w.post42_end
    GROUP BY w.start_date, w.post42_end, w.sale_days, w.post42_days
),
calc AS (
    SELECT
        pm.*,
        ROUND((pm.total_orders::numeric / pm.num_days), 2) AS orders_per_day,
        ROUND((pm.total_net_revenue / pm.num_days), 2) AS net_revenue_per_day,
        ROUND((pm.total_gross_profit / pm.num_days), 2) AS gross_profit_per_day,
        ROUND((pm.total_discount_cost / pm.num_days), 2) AS discount_cost_per_day,
        ROUND((pm.total_net_revenue / NULLIF(pm.total_orders, 0)), 2) AS aov,
        ROUND((pm.total_gross_profit / NULLIF(pm.total_net_revenue, 0) * 100), 2) AS realized_margin_pct
    FROM period_metrics pm
),
baseline AS (
    SELECT * FROM calc WHERE period_name = 'Baseline (30d)'
)
SELECT
    c.period_name,
    c.start_date,
    c.end_date,
    c.num_days,
    c.total_orders,
    c.orders_per_day,
    ROUND(c.orders_per_day - b.orders_per_day, 2) AS diff_orders_per_day,
    ROUND(((c.orders_per_day - b.orders_per_day) / b.orders_per_day * 100), 2) AS pct_lift_orders_per_day,
    c.total_net_revenue,
    c.net_revenue_per_day,
    ROUND(c.net_revenue_per_day - b.net_revenue_per_day, 2) AS diff_net_rev_per_day,
    ROUND(((c.net_revenue_per_day - b.net_revenue_per_day) / b.net_revenue_per_day * 100), 2) AS pct_lift_net_rev_per_day,
    c.total_gross_profit,
    c.gross_profit_per_day,
    ROUND(c.gross_profit_per_day - b.gross_profit_per_day, 2) AS diff_gross_profit_per_day,
    ROUND(((c.gross_profit_per_day - b.gross_profit_per_day) / b.gross_profit_per_day * 100), 2) AS pct_lift_gross_profit_per_day,
    c.aov,
    ROUND(c.aov - b.aov, 2) AS diff_aov,
    ROUND(((c.aov - b.aov) / b.aov * 100), 2) AS pct_lift_aov,
    c.realized_margin_pct,
    ROUND(c.realized_margin_pct - b.realized_margin_pct, 2) AS diff_realized_margin_pct,
    c.total_discount_cost,
    -- Total incremental metrics relative to baseline expected over the period's day count
    ROUND(c.total_net_revenue - (b.net_revenue_per_day * c.num_days), 2) AS incremental_net_revenue_total,
    ROUND(c.total_gross_profit - (b.gross_profit_per_day * c.num_days), 2) AS incremental_gross_profit_total
FROM calc c
CROSS JOIN baseline b
ORDER BY c.sort_order;

WITH customer_first_delivered AS (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id,
        MIN(o.order_date) AS first_delivered_date
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = FALSE
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY o.customer_id
),
sale_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.order_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN cfd.first_delivered_date < '2025-07-11' THEN 'existing'
            ELSE 'new'
        END AS customer_type
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN customer_first_delivered cfd ON o.customer_id = cfd.customer_id
    WHERE c.is_internal = FALSE
      AND o.status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_date BETWEEN '2025-07-11' AND '2025-07-20'
),
sale_order_items AS (
    SELECT 
        so.customer_type,
        so.customer_id,
        so.order_id,
        oi.quantity * oi.unit_price AS line_net_revenue,
        oi.quantity * p.unit_cost AS line_cost,
        oi.quantity * (p.list_price - oi.unit_price) AS line_discount_cost
    FROM sale_orders so
    JOIN public.order_items oi ON so.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN public.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
),
customer_summary AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_type,
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS distinct_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS distinct_orders,
        SUM(line_net_revenue) AS net_revenue,
        SUM(line_net_revenue - line_cost) AS gross_profit,
        SUM(line_discount_cost) AS discount_cost
    FROM sale_order_items
    GROUP BY customer_type
),
totals AS (
    SELECT 
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_customers,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders,
        SUM(line_net_revenue) AS total_net_revenue,
        SUM(line_net_revenue - line_cost) AS total_gross_profit,
        SUM(line_discount_cost) AS total_discount_cost
    FROM sale_order_items
)
SELECT 
    cs.customer_type,
    cs.distinct_customers,
    ROUND(cs.distinct_customers::numeric / t.total_customers * 100, 2) AS customer_share_pct,
    cs.distinct_orders,
    ROUND(cs.distinct_orders::numeric / t.total_orders * 100, 2) AS order_share_pct,
    ROUND(cs.net_revenue, 2) AS net_revenue,
    ROUND(cs.net_revenue / t.total_net_revenue * 100, 2) AS net_revenue_share_pct,
    ROUND(cs.gross_profit, 2) AS gross_profit,
    ROUND(cs.gross_profit / t.total_gross_profit * 100, 2) AS gross_profit_share_pct,
    ROUND(cs.discount_cost, 2) AS discount_cost,
    ROUND(cs.discount_cost / t.total_discount_cost * 100, 2) AS discount_cost_share_pct,
    ROUND(cs.net_revenue / cs.distinct_orders, 2) AS aov,
    ROUND((cs.gross_profit / cs.net_revenue) * 100, 2) AS realized_margin_pct,
    t.total_customers,
    t.total_orders,
    ROUND(t.total_net_revenue, 2) AS total_net_revenue,
    ROUND(t.total_gross_profit, 2) AS total_gross_profit,
    ROUND(t.total_discount_cost, 2) AS total_discount_cost
FROM customer_summary cs
CROSS JOIN totals t
ORDER BY cs.customer_type;

raw_report_call.summary: The July Summer Sale generated substantial short-term volume and remained net profitable overall, but heavily subsidized existing customers and induced a post-sale slump. During the 10-day sale, net revenue per day rose by 123.28% (from 4339.11 to 9688.41) and gross profit per day rose by 75.75% (from 2487.71 to 4372.21), generating 43722.10 in total gross profit. However, realized margin declined from 57.33% to 45.13%, incurring 29927.90 in list-price discount costs. Following the promotion, a post-sale dip emerged across all measured horizons: gross profit per day fell below baseline by -4.53% across 14 days (-1577.69 incremental gross profit), -8.52% across 28 days (-5932.93 incremental gross profit), and -6.92% across 42 days (-7233.97 incremental gross profit). When combining the sale and the full 42-day post-sale period (52 days total), the net incremental gross profit remained positive at 11611.03, alongside net incremental revenue of 40620.23. Furthermore, existing customers represented 78.98% of buyers (793 of 1004) and absorbed 81.81% of discount costs (24485.35 of 29927.90), showing that the promotion primarily pulled forward existing demand. Assumptions: Baseline window of 30 days (2025-06-11 to 2025-07-10) and post-sale window of 42 days (2025-07-21 to 2025-08-31) were derived from brand analysis settings; 14-day and 28-day post-sale horizons follow standard promotion evaluation methodology.

findings.claim: The July Summer Sale (promo code SUMMER25) ran for 10 days from 2025-07-11 to 2025-07-20 offering a 25.00% discount.
During the 10-day sale, net revenue per day was 9688.41 compared to 4339.11 during the 30-day baseline, representing a 123.28% lift in net revenue per day.
During the 10-day sale, gross profit per day was 4372.21 compared to 2487.71 during the baseline, an increase of 1884.50 per day or a 75.75% lift in gross profit per day.
Realized margin percentage fell from 57.33% in the baseline to 45.13% during the sale, a drop of 12.20 percentage points, while average order value fell from 106.09 to 85.97.
Total discount cost during the 10-day sale was 29927.90 across 1127 delivered orders.

In the post-sale periods, orders per day dropped below baseline by -4.30% in the 14-day post-sale window (39.14 orders per day), -8.22% in the 28-day window (37.54 orders per day), and -7.60% in the 42-day window (37.79 orders per day).

In the post-sale periods, gross profit per day dropped below baseline by -4.53% across 14 days (incremental gross profit of -1577.69), -8.52% across 28 days (incremental gross profit of -5932.93), and -6.92% across 42 days (incremental gross profit of -7233.97).

When combining the sale with post-sale windows, cumulative incremental gross profit remained positive at 17267.31 over 24 days (Sale + Post 14d), 12912.07 over 38 days (Sale + Post 28d), and 11611.03 over 52 days (Sale + Post 42d).

Existing customers accounted for 793 of the 1004 buyers (78.98% customer share), 899 of the 1127 orders (79.77% order share), 79005.65 of the 96884.10 net revenue (81.55% revenue share), and 24485.35 of the 29927.90 discount cost (81.81% discount cost share).
New customers accounted for 211 of the 1004 buyers (21.02% customer share), generating 17878.45 in net revenue and absorbing 5442.55 of discount cost.

Following the promotion, a post-sale dip emerged across all measured horizons: gross profit per day fell below baseline by -4.53% across 14 days (-1577.69 incremental gross profit), -8.52% across 28 days (-5932.93 incremental gross profit), and -6.92% across 42 days (-7233.97 incremental gross profit). Furthermore, existing customers represented 78.98% of buyers (793 of 1004) and absorbed 81.81% of discount costs (24485.35 of 29927.90), showing that the promotion primarily pulled forward existing demand. Assumptions: Baseline window of 30 days (2025-06-11 to 2025-07-10) and post-sale window of 42 days (2025-07-21 to 2025-08-31) were derived from brand analysis settings; 14-day and 28-day post-sale horizons follow standard promotion evaluation methodology.

Realized margin percentage fell from 57.33% in the baseline to 45.13% during the sale, a drop of 12.20 percentage points, while average order value fell from 106.09 to 85.97.
Total discount cost during the 10-day sale was 29927.90 across 1127 delivered orders.

In the post-sale periods, orders per day dropped below baseline by -4.30% in the 14-day post-sale window (39.14 orders per day), -8.22% in the 28-day window (37.54 orders per day), and -7.60% in the 42-day window (37.79 orders per day).

In the post-sale periods, gross profit per day dropped below baseline by -4.53% across 14 days (incremental gross profit of -1577.69), -8.52% across 28 days (incremental gross profit of -5932.93), and -6.92% across 42 days (incremental gross profit of -7233.97).

When combining the sale with post-sale windows, cumulative incremental gross profit remained positive at 17267.31 over 24 days (Sale + Post 14d), 12912.07 over 38 days (Sale + Post 28d), and 11611.03 over 52 days (Sale + Post 42d).
